allOf.description: Inherits shared step-base properties ($schema, id, owner, created_at, canonical_refs_used).

terms.description: Array of domain-specific terms with definitions, used to establish shared vocabulary across specs.

items.description: A single glossary term with its definition, domain classification, and canonical references.

term_id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this glossary term. Convention: term-{domain}-{noun}. Examples: 'term-billing-reconciliation', 'term-auth-session-token', 'term-payment-settlement'. The domain segment should match the 'domain' field value. Must be stable — downstream steps reference this ID in trace links. Anti-pattern: 'term-1', 'term-concept-a' — sequential labels cannot be traced to meaning.

term.description: The glossary term being defined. Use the canonical form of the term as it appears in project documentation. Capitalization should match usage: capitalize proper nouns and acronyms (e.g., 'JWT Token', 'REST API'), lowercase common technical terms ('endpoint', 'payload'). The term should be a noun or noun phrase. Avoid defining verbs or phrases.

acronym.description: Optional uppercase acronym or abbreviation for this term (e.g., 'JWT' for JSON Web Token, 'API' for Application Programming Interface). Must be 2+ uppercase letters/digits. Include only if the acronym (1) appears ≥3 times in project documentation or code, OR (2) is standard industry usage that any practitioner would know. Examples of valid inclusions: 'JWT' (industry standard, appears in all auth flows), 'PII' (regulatory term used throughout compliance sections), 'API' (foundational term). Examples of when to omit: 'MP' for 'Monthly Payment' that appears only once; 'CCO' for an internal role title never referenced in code. Anti-pattern: including every capitalised phrase in the spec — acronyms should genuinely save space and reduce ambiguity.

definition.description: Clear, precise definition of the term as used in THIS project. Must be at least 20 characters (enforced by minLength). Should: (1) define the term without using the term itself, (2) distinguish it from similar terms in the domain, (3) be specific to the project context rather than a generic dictionary definition. Example: 'A short-lived cryptographic credential issued by the authentication service upon successful login, valid for 15 minutes. Distinct from the refresh_token which is long-lived.' Avoid: circular definitions, vague descriptions, generic Wikipedia-style prose.

domain.description: Optional knowledge domain or subdomain this term belongs to. Use lowercase-alphabetic kebab-case (no digits) (e.g., 'billing', 'auth', 'user-management'). Unlike standard kebabId, domain values must not contain digits (enforced by pattern). While optional, providing a domain helps organise large glossaries and improves canonical canon clustering. If provided, each term should belong to exactly one domain. Decision rule: assign the domain where the term was first introduced, not all domains where it is used. Example: 'settlement-period' — first introduced in the billing domain, used in reporting too — domain='billing'. Wrong: domain='auth2' (digits not allowed), domain='general' (too broad), domain='billing-reporting' (pick one primary domain). Decision rules: 'authentication' for login/session terms, 'billing' for payment/invoice terms, 'data-processing' for ETL/pipeline terms, 'product' for cross-cutting business terms. Examples: term 'session-token' → domain 'authentication'; term 'invoice-line-item' → domain 'billing'. Anti-pattern: assigning domain='general' or domain='common' to avoid making a choice — pick the domain where the term has the most specific meaning; 'general', 'misc', 'all' prevent linter grouping and downstream filtering.

units.description: Unit of measurement if this term represents a measurable quantity. Use standard abbreviations (e.g., 'ms' for milliseconds, 'MB/s' for megabytes per second, 'req/s' for requests per second). Only include when the term has a natural numeric unit; omit for non-quantitative terms.

term_ref.description: Canonical reference to the canon entry for this term. Kind must be 'term'. Example: {"id": "cn:project:term:billing-reconciliation", "kind": "term", "label": "billing reconciliation"}. The id must match an entry in canon/manifest.json, or a canonical_proposals entry must be added. This is the primary mechanism for promoting a glossary term to the shared vocabulary. Validated by canonical-integrity lint.

acronym_ref.description: Canonical reference to the canon entry for the acronym form of this term. Kind must be 'acronym'. Example: {"id": "cn:project:acronym:jwt", "kind": "acronym", "label": "JWT"}. Only present when the 'acronym' field is also set. Links the short form to the same concept as term_ref, ensuring the acronym resolves to the canonical definition. Validated by canonical-integrity lint.

unit_ref.description: Canonical reference to the unit of measurement for this term. Kind is structurally pinned to 'unit'. Example: {"id": "cn:core:unit:ms", "kind": "unit"} for milliseconds. Only present when the 'units' field is also set — they must be consistent. Common unit IDs: cn:core:unit:ms, cn:core:unit:percent, cn:core:unit:count. Validated by canonical-integrity lint.
